description: Modeled lifetime probability of developing endometrial cancer for a 50-year-old woman with BMI 40 or greater assigned to usual care (no prevention strategy); a Markov-model output (not a raw incidence rate) combining SEER age-specific incidence with obesity hazard ratios
source: Dottino JA, Hasselblad V, Secord AA, Myers ER, Chino J, Havrilesky LJ. 'Levonorgestrel Intrauterine Device as an Endometrial Cancer Prevention Strategy in Obese Women: A Cost-Effectiveness Analysis.' Obstet Gynecol. 2016;128(4):747-753. PDF read directly 2026-09-10. Results: 'For a 50-year-old woman with a BMI 40 or greater assigned to usual care, there is a 3% lifetime probability of developing... endometrial cancer.'
notes: Population mismatch, flagged explicitly: Dottino's Markov model starts a 50-year-old woman with no prior intervention; this project's population is reproductive-age (typically 20s-40s) women undergoing bariatric surgery, a materially younger cohort with a longer remaining time horizon and (per bariatric_surgery_endometrial_cancer_hazard_ratio) a large weight-loss-driven risk reduction Dottino's model does not include at all. Used here only as the best available anchor for 'obese, untreated' lifetime endometrial cancer risk, not as a bariatric-surgery-population-specific estimate. See docs/data_sources.md for the full reasoning chain.

description: Modeled lifetime probability of developing endometrial cancer for a 50-year-old woman with BMI 30 or greater assigned to usual care (no prevention strategy); a Markov-model output combining SEER age-specific incidence with obesity hazard ratios
source: Dottino JA, et al. Obstet Gynecol. 2016;128(4):747-753. PDF read directly 2026-09-10. Results: 'For a 50-year-old woman with a BMI 30 or greater assigned to usual care, there is a 1.9% lifetime probability of developing... endometrial cancer.'
notes: Same population-mismatch caveat as endometrial_cancer_lifetime_risk_usual_care_bmi40. BMI 30+ is a much broader, lower-risk group than this project's actual population (bariatric-surgery candidates typically have BMI 35-40+); retained mainly for context/comparison, not as this module's primary estimate.

description: Hazard ratio for endometrial cancer incidence among bariatric-surgery patients compared with matched non-surgical patients with severe obesity, from a large multisite retrospective cohort
source: Schauer DP, Feigelson HS, Koebnick C, Caan B, Weinmann S, Leonard AC, Powers JD, Yenumula PR, Arterburn DE. 'Bariatric Surgery and the Risk of Cancer in a Large Multisite Cohort.' Ann Surg. 2019;269(1):95-101. doi:10.1097/SLA.0000000000002525. Directly verified via the open-access PMC full text (PMC6201282), 2026-09-10: 'endometrial (HR 0.50, 95% C.I. 0.37, 0.67, P<0.001)... were... statistically significantly lower among those who had undergone bariatric surgery compared to matched non-surgical patients.' Retrospective cohort, 5 US integrated health systems (Kaiser Permanente Colorado/Southern California/Northern California/Northwest, University of Cincinnati), 22,198 bariatric-surgery patients matched to 66,427 non-surgical patients with severe obesity on sex, age, site, BMI, and Elixhauser comorbidity index; surgery 2005-2012, follow-up through 2014 (up to 10 years).
notes: This is the single most population-relevant number in this module: unlike the Dottino lifetime-risk figures above, this cohort directly compares bariatric-surgery patients with severely obese non-surgical patients, the actual comparison this project's population faces. Used as the multiplier applied to the untreated-obese baseline risk to get a bariatric-surgery-specific 'usual care' risk, before the IUD's own additional effect is applied.

description: Standardized incidence ratio (observed-to-expected) for endometrial adenocarcinoma among levonorgestrel-releasing IUD users compared with the general population, from a large national cohort
source: Soini T, Hurskainen R, Grenman S, Maenpaa J, Paavonen J, Pukkala E. 'Cancer risk in women using the levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system in Finland.' Obstet Gynecol. 2014;124(2 pt 1):292-299. doi:10.1097/AOG.0000000000000356. Directly verified via the PubMed/Europe PMC abstract, 2026-09-10: 'The standardized incidence ratio... for endometrial adenocarcinoma was 0.50 (95% CI 0.35-0.70; 34 observed compared with 68 expected cases) after the first levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system purchase.' All Finnish women aged 30-49 using an LNG-IUS for menorrhagia treatment in 1994-2007 (n=93,843), followed 855,324 women-years (mean approximately 9.1 years/woman), linked to the Finnish Cancer Registry.
notes: Independently corroborated: this same 0.50 figure is the risk-reduction assumption used by two subsequent peer-reviewed obesity-specific LNG-IUD cost-effectiveness models, Dottino et al. 2016 (Obstet Gynecol, read directly for this project) and Bernard et al. 2021 (Gynecol Oncol 161:367-373, abstract directly verified 2026-09-10), so this is not a one-off, uncorroborated estimate. Caveat: Soini's cohort used the IUD for menorrhagia treatment, not routine contraception, and no RCT with a cancer endpoint exists for this device (would be difficult ethically and require decades of follow-up); this remains an observational-cohort estimate, not a causal-trial result.

description: Number of years the IUD's endometrial-cancer risk reduction is assumed to apply while the device remains in place, as used by the source literature's own base case
source: Base value (5 years) is Dottino et al. 2016's explicitly-stated modeling assumption, not a direct empirical finding: 'We assumed that the protective effect of the IUD would last for the 5 years that the IUD was in place.' High value (8 years) is Liletta's current FDA-labeled duration of use (the same device this project's cost model prices), within Soini et al. 2014's actual mean cohort follow-up of approximately 9.1 years (855,324 women-years / 93,843 women). Bernard et al. 2021 (Gynecol Oncol 161:367-373) independently modeled LNG-IUS protective durations up to 14 years (7 years, replaced once) using the same risk-reduction figure.
notes: NOT currently consumed by compute_cancer_prevention_summary(): that function applies the incidence ratio directly to a LIFETIME baseline risk (age 50 to 100 in Dottino's model), which implicitly assumes the protective effect operates across the full remaining lifetime rather than only this 5-8 year window. This makes the module's headline estimate a likely-optimistic upper bound, not a duration-corrected figure. Retained here as a documented, real number for context and as the natural next parameter a future annual (rather than lifetime) Markov-style version of this module would need. See docs/data_sources.md, 'Cancer-prevention estimate' section, for the full explanation of this simplification.
